name: Update the casks

# Every 15 minutes, Casks/pinky.rb becomes the cask that Pinky's latest
# release carries (pinky.rb, which its release workflow writes) when that
# one is newer, so Pinky's workflow needs no token for this repository.
# This file comes from scripts/release/homebrew-tap/ in DIYgod/pinky, which
# `scripts/release.sh setup` copies here.
#
# GitHub turns off schedules after 60 days without a commit here: a release
# in that time keeps it on, and "Run workflow" brings it back.
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "7,22,37,52 * * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: update

jobs:
  pinky:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Take the cask of Pinky's latest release
        run: |
          url=https://github.com/DIYgod/pinky/releases/latest/download/pinky.rb
          if ! curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/pinky.rb" "$url"; then
            echo "No release with a cask at $url yet."
            exit 0
          fi
          version() { sed -n 's/^ *version "\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "$1" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1; }
          new=$(version "$RUNNER_TEMP/pinky.rb")
          old=$(version Casks/pinky.rb)
          case "$new" in
          [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;
          *) echo "::error::The release's pinky.rb has no version"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          ruby -c "$RUNNER_TEMP/pinky.rb" > /dev/null
          # The newer of the two, comparing each part as a number.
          newest=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$new" "${old:-0.0.0}" | sort -t . -k 1,1n -k 2,2n -k 3,3n | tail -n 1)
          if [ "$new" = "$old" ] || [ "$newest" != "$new" ]; then
            echo "Casks/pinky.rb has ${old} already."
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p Casks
          cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/pinky.rb" Casks/pinky.rb
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add Casks/pinky.rb
          git commit --quiet -m "pinky $new"
          git push --quiet
          echo "Casks/pinky.rb installs pinky $new (was ${old:-nothing})."

# DIYgod's Homebrew tap

```sh
brew install --cask diygod/tap/pinky
```

| Cask | |
| --- | --- |
| [`pinky`](Casks/pinky.rb) | [Pinky](https://github.com/DIYgod/pinky): let AI agents use your phone, with you in the loop. Also installs the `pinkyctl` command (`pinkyctl mcp`). |

The casks follow their apps' releases: a workflow takes the cask that each release of Pinky carries, within a quarter of an hour. Pinky updates itself, so `brew upgrade` leaves it alone unless you pass `--greedy`.

cask "pinky" do
  arch arm: "arm64", intel: "amd64"

  version "2026.1115.10"
  sha256 arm:   "5635cd64e594628fbaa7483192a353f7f1dc75d3ded8697585621d219746216f",
         intel: "baad32e04489257918025e77074114cfd3570db8b1b71403dfdda20172a97417"

  url "https://github.com/DIYgod/pinky/releases/download/v#{version}/pinky-#{version}-darwin-#{arch}.zip"
  name "Pinky"
  desc "Let AI agents use your phone, with you in the loop"
  homepage "https://github.com/DIYgod/pinky"

  livecheck do
    url :url
    strategy :github_latest
  end

  auto_updates true
  depends_on macos: :ventura

  app "Pinky.app"
  command_wrapper "pinkyctl",
                  executable: "#{appdir}/Pinky.app/Contents/MacOS/Pinky"

  uninstall quit: "app.pinky.desktop"

  zap trash: [
    "~/Library/Application Support/Pinky",
    "~/Library/Caches/app.pinky.desktop",
    "~/Library/HTTPStorages/app.pinky.desktop",
    "~/Library/Logs/Pinky",
    "~/Library/Preferences/app.pinky.desktop.plist",
    "~/Library/Saved Application State/app.pinky.desktop.savedState",
  ]

  caveats <<~EOS
    Agents start Pinky with: pinkyctl mcp
      claude mcp add pinky -- pinkyctl mcp
    The command was named pinky before, a name coreutils has too: change
    agents that run "pinky mcp" to run "pinkyctl mcp".
  EOS
end
